title: Log parser and summary report
instructions:
Complete two modules for parsing UTF-8 application logs and reporting counts.

## Files
- `log_parser.py`: `parse_line`, `parse_file`, and `LEVELS`.
- `log_report.py`: `summarize` and `report_file`, using the parser module.

`LEVELS` is the tuple `("INFO", "WARN", "ERROR")`.
`parse_line(line: str) -> dict | None` strips surrounding whitespace and
returns None for blank lines or lines whose first non-whitespace character
is `#`. Other lines use `timestamp | level | message`. Split on only the
first two pipes and strip each field; further pipes belong to the message.
The timestamp must be a valid date and time with exact spelling
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (years 0001–9999, seconds 00–59); levels are case
sensitive and must be in LEVELS; messages must be nonempty. Malformed records
raise `ValueError`. Return exactly the keys `timestamp`, `level`, `message`,
all strings, with the stripped timestamp preserved.

`parse_file(path: str | Path) -> tuple[list[dict], list[int]]` opens UTF-8,
returns valid records in input order and 1-based physical line numbers of
malformed records. Skip comments and blanks without marking them invalid.
Continue after bad records. Propagate filesystem errors.

`summarize(records: Iterable[dict]) -> dict` accepts valid parsed records,
including a generator, without modifying them. Return exactly `total` (int),
`counts` (a dict with all three levels even when zero), `earliest`, and
`latest` (minimum/maximum timestamp strings, or None when empty).

`report_file(path: str | Path) -> str` parses and summarizes the file. Return
exactly these seven lines, in order, with a final newline:
```
TOTAL <total>
INFO <count>
WARN <count>
ERROR <count>
FIRST <earliest timestamp or ->
LAST <latest timestamp or ->
INVALID <comma-separated invalid line numbers, no spaces, or ->
```
No error-message wording is required. Inputs have the indicated types.
